key_insight: Chance-constrained reinforcement learning sequences spacecraft inspection viewpoints while treating collision risk as an explicit design budget.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports autonomous on-orbit inspection that balances surface coverage, fuel use, and safety under navigation and manoeuvre errors.
method: Model viewpoint sequencing as a constrained Markov decision process and train with PPO.
Use Clohessy–Wiltshire relative-motion dynamics to evaluate transfers and enforce reachability and Δv limits.
Adapt the stochastic safety penalty with a PID-controlled Lagrangian multiplier.
evidence_signal: In Galileo-class satellite evaluations, policies stayed within tested risk limits and the mission Δv budget, achieved near-maximum coverage, and produced less than half the violation rate of fixed-margin deterministic planning at comparable coverage.
watch_item: Reported safety performance depends on the assumed dynamics and error distributions; robustness to model mismatch requires further validation.
paper_title: Chance-Constrained Inspection Viewpoint Sequencing for On-Orbit Servicing via Safe Reinforcement Learning
